entry.title: Порівняння провайдерів CAPTCHA для сторінок входу: reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha, Turnstile, GeeTest та Alibaba Cloud у Casdoor
entry.summary: Порівняйте reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha, Cloudflare Turnstile, GeeTest, Alibaba Cloud Captcha та вбудовану captcha для сторінок входу та реєстрації, а також дізнайтеся, як використовувати їх у Casdoor.
entry.content:
Для більшості сторінок входу та реєстрації в глобальному інтернеті найпростішим вибором є Cloudflare Turnstile: безкоштовний план не має обмежень на кількість перевірок, а його режим за замовчуванням показує прапорець лише підозрілим відвідувачам. Якщо багато ваших користувачів знаходяться в материковому Китаї, скористайтеся Alibaba Cloud Captcha або GeeTest, оскільки Cloudflare зазначає, що Turnstile там не підтримується. Якщо вам потрібна captcha, яка працює без жодних зовнішніх сервісів, використовуйте вбудовану графічну captcha Casdoor. Casdoor підтримує всі ці варіанти, а також Google reCAPTCHA (v2 та v3) і hCaptcha як провайдери капчі, і ви можете налаштувати, коли саме з'являється captcha для кожного додатка.

Порівняння​

Ціни та доступність, зазначені нижче, були перевірені на сайтах постачальників станом на 2026-11-02. Якщо постачальник не публікує конкретну цифру, у таблиці це вказано замість припущень.

Два зауваження щодо рядків reCAPTCHA. Google перемістив reCAPTCHA до Google Cloud Fraud Defense з рівнями Essentials, Premium та Enterprise, а безкоштовна квота на 10 000 оцінок розподілена між усією організацією Google Cloud. Casdoor взаємодіє з reCAPTCHA через ключ сайту та секретний ключ стандартного ендпоінту siteverify, і завантажує скрипт з recaptcha.net, а не з google.com, як для браузерного скрипту, так і для серверної перевірки.

Що обрати​

Глобальний SaaS​

Почніть з Cloudflare Turnstile. Безкоштовний план не лімітує кількість перевірок, режим Managed дозволяє більшості користувачів нічого не клікати, і вам не потрібно спрямовувати ваш сайт через Cloudflare. Якщо ви вже використовуєте Google Cloud і хочете отримати сигнали ризику від reCAPTCHA, reCAPTCHA буде чудовим вибором, але стежте за безкоштовною квотою в 10 000 оцінок: активна сторінка входу або атака на SMS-шлюз можуть вичерпати її за день. hCaptcha — інший поширений вибір; його безкоштовний план завжди показує завдання, а пасивні режими є платними.

Застосунок із користувачами в материковому Китаї​

Turnstile не підходить, згідно з документацією Cloudflare. Для reCAPTCHA Google документує www.recaptcha.net як домен для використання, коли www.google.com недоступний, і Casdoor вже використовує його, але вам все одно варто протестувати з мереж ваших користувачів перед тим, як покладатися на це. hCaptcha не публікує жодних заяв щодо Китаю, тому тут діють ті самі поради.

Два надійні варіанти — це Alibaba Cloud Captcha та GeeTest. Alibaba Cloud публікує ціни за виклик і дозволяє почати з моделі оплати за використання; його режим без слідів (у Casdoor використовуйте підтип Popup) наближається до невидимого досвіду Turnstile. GeeTest продається через відділ продажів після 30-денного пробного періоду. Якщо ви обслуговуєте і Китай, і решту світу з одного Casdoor, пам'ятайте, що один додаток може мати лише одного провайдера капчі, тому розділіть аудиторії на два додатки, якщо їм потрібні різні капчі.

Користувачі в ЄС, чутливі до приватності​

Кожна хостингова капча надсилає певні дані про браузер відвідувача постачальнику. Якщо ваш юридичний відділ хоче повністю виключити третіх сторінів із шляху входу, то типова капча Casdoor — єдиний варіант у таблиці, який зберігає все на вашому власному сервері. Серед хостингових рішень і Turnstile, і hCaptcha позиціонують конфіденційність як частину продукту (дані обмежені тим, що потрібно для перевірки; відповідно GDPR та EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework). reCAPTCHA встановлює cookie _GRECAPTCHA; Google зазначає, що використання www.recaptcha.net дозволяє уникнути інших cookie, які може встановлювати www.google.com. Який би варіант ви не обрали, додайте його до вашого повідомлення про конфіденційність.

Self-hosted, інтранет або офлайн-режим​

Використовуйте типову капчу. Їй не потрібні ключі та вихідний мережевий доступ, тому вона працює в ізольованих середовищах (air-gapped). Поєднайте її з правилом Internet-Only (нижче), щоб користувачі в офісній мережі ніколи не бачили її, а запити з публічного інтернету продовжували її отримувати.

Типова капча є найслабшою з групи проти автоматизованих солверів, оскільки це звичайне зображення спотворених цифр. Для публічної сторінки входу з високим трафіком поєднайте її з багатофакторною автентифікацією або переведіть користувачів на вхід без пароля, що усунує перебір паролів, уповільненням якого й займаються капчі.

Як CAPTCHA працює в Casdoor​

Ви додаєте провайдера з Category, встановленою в Captcha, та одним із цих типів: Default, reCAPTCHA, reCAPTCHA v2, reCAPTCHA v3, hCaptcha, Cloudflare Turnstile, GEETEST або Aliyun Captcha. Потім додаєте його до застосунку на вкладці Providers. Застосунок може містити лише одного провайдера капчі; Casdoor відмовиться зберігати другого. Кроки налаштування для кожного постачальника описано в документації провайдерів капчі.

Де Casdoor запитує капчу​

Той самий провайдер захищає кілька дій, і Casdoor перевіряє токен на сервері, а не лише в браузері:

  • Вхід за паролем.
  • Надсилання форми реєстрації.
  • Надсилання кода верифікації через електронну пошту або SMS, що охоплює крок підтвердження при реєстрації, сторінку відновлення пароля та вхід за кодом. Це захист від ботів, які витрачають ваш бюджет на SMS.

Коли Casdoor запитує капчу​

Правило Rule провайдера капчі в застосунку визначає, коли вона з’являється:

RuleBehavior
NoneНіколи; капча вимкнена
DynamicЛише після того, як кількість невдалих спроб входу користувача досягне значення Failed signin limit застосунку
AlwaysЩоразу
Internet-OnlyДля запитів із публічних IP-адрес; не для приватних, loopback чи інших непублічних адрес

Dynamic — найм’якший параметр для входу: чесні користувачі ніколи не бачать завдання, а той, хто перебирає паролі, стикається з ним після кількох невдалих спроб. Однак це стосується лише вже існуючих облікових записів. Реєстрація або надсилання кода на адресу, яка ще не має облікового запису, не активує його. Якщо вас турбує зловживання SMS або електронною поштою під час реєстрації, використовуйте Always або Internet-Only.

Де вона з’являється на сторінці​

У пунктах входу застосунку елемент Captcha має своє власне правило: Pop up показує капчу в діалоговому вікні, коли вона потрібна, а Inline розміщує її безпосередньо на сторінці. Див. Зміна капчі. Alibaba Cloud Captcha має додатковий Sub type: Embed показує її всередині діалогового вікна Casdoor, а Popup передає управління власному вспливаючому вікну Alibaba Cloud, що необхідно для сценаріїв без трасування (traceless).

Використовуйте кнопку Preview на сторінці провайдера, щоб перевірити ключі перед увімкненням правила.

entry.title: Customize the Login Page in Casdoor: Custom Styling of the Authentication UI Without Forking
entry.summary: Style Casdoor's hosted login and sign-up pages without forking: themes, CSS, HTML, logo, background, form position, sign-in fields and organization choice.
entry.content:
Yes, Casdoor supports custom styling of its authentication UI, and you don't need to fork the frontend to get it. Every application has a UI Customization tab where you set the logo, favicon, background image, custom CSS for desktop and mobile, the position of the form, a side panel, footer HTML and a theme. Two tables, Signin items and Signup items, decide which fields the login and sign-up pages show, in which order, with which labels and placeholders. All of it is stored per application in the database, so one Casdoor instance can serve many differently branded login pages, and organization admins can edit their own pages within safe limits.

What to change and where​

What you want to changeWhere in CasdoorDocs
Primary color, corner radius, dark or compact styleTheme of the organization, or of the application with Follow organization theme offCustomize the theme
A complete ready-made lookIdentity → Marketplace, sign-in themesMarketplace
Logo, dark logo, favicon, page titleApplication edit pageApplication settings
Background image (desktop and phone)Background URL, Background URL MobileUI customization
Look of the formCustom CSS, Custom CSS MobileUI customization
Form on the left, center or right, or next to a panelForm position, Side panel HTMLUI customization
Text below the formFooter HTMLApplication settings
Which fields the login page shows, order, placeholdersSignin itemsSign-in items table
Password, code, magic link, WebAuthn, LDAP and their orderSignin methodsSign-in methods
Sign-up fields, required flags, labels, regexSignup itemsSign-up items table
Language selectorLanguages sign-in item, Languages of the organizationSign-in items table
Let users pick or type their organizationOrg choice modeSpecify login organization

In the Chinese console the tab is called 界面定制 and the sign-in table 登录项, so if you are looking for how to change the 登录界面 of an application, start there.

Themes: organization, application and Marketplace​

The quickest change is the theme. A theme in Casdoor is a small object with a style (Default, Dark, Document or Blossom in the editor), a primary color, a border radius and a compact switch. You can set it on the organization, where it applies to the console for its members and to the entry pages of every application that follows the organization theme, or on a single application by turning off Follow organization theme. The application edit page has a live preview, so you can see the result before you save.

If you want more than colors, the Casdoor Marketplace has sign-in themes. Installing one writes the theme data, form position, form CSS for desktop and mobile, side panel HTML, footer HTML and background URLs of one application. The casdoor-integrations repository currently holds 24 themes, from Midnight and Split to Terminal, Nord and Solarized. Uninstalling a theme restores what the application had before, so trying one costs nothing. Browse them at marketplace.casdoor.com.

Branding: logo, favicon and background​

Each application has its own Logo, Favicon and Title, separate from the organization. One organization can run several products that share users but show different logos. There is also an optional Logo dark, shown when the page is in dark mode; without it, Casdoor keeps using the normal logo.

Background URL sets the image behind the form. Set Background URL Mobile too if the desktop image crops badly on phones. The preview updates as soon as the URL loads.

Custom CSS and form layout​

Custom CSS takes plain CSS rules; Casdoor wraps them in a style element itself, so don't add one of your own. The main containers to target are .login-panel and .login-form:

.login-panel {
  border-radius: 12px;
  background-color: #ffffff;
  box-shadow: 0 0 30px 20px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2);
}

Custom CSS Mobile holds rules for phones, so you don't need to write media queries for the common case.

Form position places the form on the left, center or right. The fourth option, Enable side panel, centers the form and puts a panel next to it whose content comes from Side panel HTML. That field takes HTML, so a style element inside it is fine.

Footer HTML is rendered below the sign-in and sign-up forms. If the application is the default application of its organization, its footer also replaces "Powered by Casdoor" in the admin console for that organization's users.

When you are happy with a design on staging, Export JSON at the bottom of the application edit page copies the look (logo, favicon, backgrounds, CSS, form position, side panel, theme and the custom HTML fields) to the clipboard, and Import JSON on the same application on another instance applies it. The export contains no secrets or providers.

Fields, labels and order​

The Signin items table lists every element of the login page: the logo, the username and password fields, the forgot-password link, the agreement checkbox, the language selector, the captcha, provider buttons and so on. For each row you can set Visible, a custom Placeholder, per-item Custom CSS and a rule, and move it up or down. You can also add custom items whose label is HTML.

A few rules worth knowing:

  • Hiding Forgot password? turns off password reset in the API too, not just the link.
  • The Captcha rule switches between a pop-up and an inline captcha. If you are choosing a captcha provider, see CAPTCHA providers compared for login pages.
  • The Languages rule switches between a globe icon and a labeled selector. The list itself is limited to the Languages of the organization, so an organization that only serves English and Japanese users shows only those two.

The sign-in methods (password, verification code, magic link, WebAuthn, LDAP, Face ID and others) are a separate table, Signin methods, with its own order and display names.

The Signup items table does the same for registration, with Required, Regex validation, custom Label and rules such as "No verification" for email. POST /api/signup also clears every field whose item is hidden, so API clients can't set fields your form doesn't show. Prompted asks users for missing fields, such as a phone number, after they sign in through a provider that didn't supply one.

Specify the login organization​

If several organizations share one Casdoor, users need a way to reach the right one. Org choice mode on the default application of an organization (or on app-built-in) adds an organization step to /login: Input shows a text field, Select shows a dropdown. After the user picks, Casdoor sends them to /login/<organization>, which shows that organization's own styled page. The browser remembers the last organization in localStorage, so a user whose console session expired lands on their own login page again.

What tenant admins can safely change​

Letting every customer style their own login page raises an obvious question: what stops an organization admin from adding a script that copies passwords, or a CSS selector that leaks each typed character through background image requests? Casdoor checks this on the server. When an admin who is not a global admin adds or saves an application, every custom HTML and CSS field that changed is validated, and the save is rejected if any of them breaks the rules:

  • HTML may only use layout and text elements such as div, span, p, headings, lists, links, images, tables, style and basic SVG shapes. script, form, input and iframe are refused, as are on... event handlers, srcset, formaction, srcdoc and similar attributes. href is allowed only on links with relative, http, https, mailto or tel URLs.
  • CSS may not contain backslashes, <, image(, image-set( and a few other functions. Every url() must be relative, a data: URL, or start with an allowed prefix: Google Fonts, Fontsource on jsDelivr, the Casdoor CDNs, this Casdoor's own origin, the domains of the global storage providers, or an entry of formCssAllowedUrls.
  • @import is allowed only from Google Fonts and Fontsource, because an imported stylesheet isn't checked itself.

To let tenants load images from your own host, add it to conf/app.conf (see Configuration):

formCssAllowedUrls = "https://img.example.com/"

On top of the save-time check, the sign-in pages sanitize custom HTML before rendering it, unless the application belongs to the built-in organization or a global admin has turned on Enable custom scripts for it. Only a global admin can turn that switch on, and while it is on only a global admin can change that application's HTML. The same rules apply when a tenant installs a Marketplace theme: a theme that breaks them can only be installed by a global admin.

Signin HTML and Signup HTML deserve a separate note: they replace the whole built-in page, form included. Since tenants can't add forms or scripts, these two fields are mainly for global admins; for branding, CSS, the side panel and the footer are the better tools.

Hosted login page or your own UI?​

You can build your own login screen on Casdoor's API, but the hosted page is usually the better choice. With OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect, users type their password only on the Casdoor origin and your application receives an authorization code, never the credentials. Captcha, MFA, social and enterprise providers, forgot-password, sign-up validation and the organization picker keep working without code on your side, and they keep getting fixes when you upgrade Casdoor. A custom UI has to reimplement each of those flows and puts passwords through your own servers. Guides for wiring the hosted page into an app: Spring Boot SSO with OIDC and Nginx SSO authentication.

Other hosted providers make the same trade. Idura Verify, for example, lets you add a stylesheet URL and custom HTML around its login box from its dashboard, under a strict Content Security Policy with an explicit list of style origins for fonts and images. Casdoor's formCssAllowedUrls plays the same role, with the difference that Casdoor is open source and self-hosted, so you control the list.

entry.title: Jenkins OIDC, Gitea OIDC and Grafana SSO with Casdoor: One Login for a Self-Hosted DevOps Stack
entry.summary: Use Casdoor as the OIDC provider for Gitea, Jenkins, Grafana, Argo CD, MinIO, Portainer, Harbor and GitLab: callback URLs, config keys and admin group mapping.
entry.content:
Every tool in a typical self-hosted DevOps stack can act as an OpenID Connect client: Gitea and Argo CD speak OIDC natively, Jenkins does through the oic-auth plugin, Grafana and Portainer through generic OAuth 2.0, and MinIO, Harbor and GitLab through their OIDC settings. Point all of them at one Casdoor instance, give each tool its own Casdoor application, and put your people in Casdoor groups. Each tool then reads the groups claim and decides who is an administrator. This post lists the callback URL, the config keys and the group mapping for each tool, then covers the parts they share.

The stack at a glance​

All paths below are relative to the tool's own public URL. Register them in Redirect URLs of the Casdoor application for that tool.

AppProtocolCallback URLGroup/role to admin mappingCasdoor doc
GiteaOIDC (OAuth2 auth source)/user/oauth2/<source-name>/callbackYes: admin group, restricted group, team mapGitea
JenkinsOIDC (oic-auth plugin)/securityRealm/finishLogin, logout /OicLogoutYes: groups claim plus Matrix-based securityJenkins (OIDC)
GrafanaGeneric OAuth 2.0/login/generic_oauthYes: role_attribute_pathGrafana
Argo CDOIDC/auth/callback, CLI http://localhost:8085/auth/callbackYes: argocd-rbac-cmArgo CD
MinIOOIDCConsole /oauth_callbackPolicies from one claim (claim_name)MinIO
PortainerOAuth 2.0 (Custom)The Portainer base URLBusiness Edition onlyPortainer
HarborOIDC/c/oidc/callbackYes: OIDC Admin Groupnone yet
GitLabOIDC (OmniAuth)/users/auth/openid_connect/callbackPremium and Ultimate: admin_groupsGitLab

The discovery document every OIDC client needs is https://<casdoor-host>/.well-known/openid-configuration. If you have not connected an OIDC client to Casdoor before, Connect a standard OIDC client explains the endpoints.

Prepare Casdoor once​

Before touching the tools, set up three things in Casdoor.

Groups. Create groups such as devops-admins and devops-users in the organization tree and add users to them. See Groups.

Token group format. By default the groups claim names each group as <organization>/<group>. Most tools compare the claim with a plain string you type, so set Token group format on the OIDC/OAuth tab of each application to Name (group). The claim then carries devops-admins. The options are described under Group format.

Token format. Keep Token format at JWT, the default. In that format the ID token carries groups, roles and tag. JWT-Empty and JWT-Standard leave all three out of the token, and JWT-Custom carries them only if you select them in Token fields. The /api/userinfo response returns groups and the role names when the profile scope is granted, so tools that read userinfo still see them.

Roles work too. In the JWT format the roles claim is an array of role objects, so match on roles[*].name. In /api/userinfo it is a plain array of names. See User roles.

Gitea​

In Site Administration, add an authentication source of type OAuth2 with provider OpenID Connect, the client ID and secret, and the Casdoor discovery URL. The name you give the source is part of the callback URL: a source named casdoor uses https://gitea.example.com/user/oauth2/casdoor/callback.

For group mapping, fill in Claim name providing group names with groups, then Group Claim value for administrator users with devops-admins. Gitea also has Group Claim value for restricted users and Map claimed groups to Organization teams. The same source from the CLI:

gitea admin auth add-oauth \
  --name casdoor \
  --provider openidConnect \
  --key <client-id> \
  --secret <client-secret> \
  --auto-discover-url https://door.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration \
  --group-claim-name groups \
  --admin-group devops-admins

Jenkins​

Jenkins has no OIDC support of its own. Install the OpenId Connect Authentication plugin, choose it as the security realm, and use the well-known configuration. The login callback is /securityRealm/finishLogin and the logout callback is /OicLogout; add both to Casdoor. In JCasC:

jenkins:
  securityRealm:
    oic:
      serverConfiguration:
        wellKnown:
          wellKnownOpenIDConfigurationUrl: https://door.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration
      clientId: <client-id>
      clientSecret: <client-secret>
      userNameField: name
      fullNameFieldName: displayName
      emailFieldName: email
      groupsFieldName: groups
      logoutFromOpenidProvider: true
      properties:
      - "pkce"

The plugin only passes the groups to Jenkins. Rights come from the authorization strategy: with Matrix-based security, each row of the table is a user or a group, so add a row for devops-admins and give it Overall/Administer. Choosing the plugin as the security realm turns off other login methods, so configure the plugin's escapeHatch property (a fallback username and secret) before you save. Casdoor also has its own Jenkins plugin, described in Jenkins plugin, but the generic OIDC plugin is the one this post assumes.

Grafana​

Grafana uses generic OAuth. Its callback is /login/generic_oauth. Grafana's default scopes is user:email, so set the OIDC scopes explicitly:

[auth.generic_oauth]
enabled = true
name = Casdoor
client_id = <client-id>
client_secret = <client-secret>
scopes = openid profile email
auth_url = https://door.example.com/login/oauth/authorize
token_url = https://door.example.com/api/login/oauth/access_token
api_url = https://door.example.com/api/userinfo
use_pkce = true
groups_attribute_path = groups
role_attribute_path = contains(groups[*], 'devops-admins') && 'Admin' || contains(groups[*], 'devops-users') && 'Editor' || 'Viewer'
role_attribute_strict = true

Grafana evaluates role_attribute_path against the ID token first, then the userinfo response, then the access token. Valid results are None, Viewer, Editor, Admin and GrafanaAdmin; the last one needs allow_assign_grafana_admin = true. allowed_groups limits login to listed groups and requires groups_attribute_path. Team sync is a Grafana Enterprise and Grafana Cloud feature.

Argo CD​

Argo CD talks to Casdoor directly, without its bundled Dex. The browser callback is /auth/callback. argocd login --sso starts a local server on port 8085 by default and uses http://localhost:8085/auth/callback, so register that as well.

Set url and oidc.config (with name, issuer, clientID, clientSecret, requestedScopes) in argocd-cm. Argo CD's default requestedScopes adds a groups scope. Casdoor does not need it, because the JWT ID token always carries groups, so our guide requests ["openid", "profile", "email"]. Groups are mapped in argocd-rbac-cm, where scopes defaults to [groups]:

data:
  policy.default: role:readonly
  policy.csv: |
    g, devops-admins, role:admin

The full walkthrough, including the client secret in argocd-secret, is in the Argo CD guide.

MinIO​

MinIO reads policies from a single claim, set with claim_name (default policy). It does not map groups. MinIO's own Casdoor quickstart and our guide use Casdoor's tag claim: put a MinIO policy name such as readwrite in the user's Tag, then:

mc admin config set myminio identity_openid \
  config_url="https://door.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration" \
  client_id=<client-id> client_secret=<client-secret> claim_name="tag"

role_policy is the alternative: every user who signs in through this provider gets the listed policies, and it cannot be combined with claim_name. The Console callback is <console-url>/oauth_callback. Behind a proxy, set MINIO_BROWSER_REDIRECT_URL; the old redirect_uri key is deprecated. Note that the minio/minio GitHub repository has been archived and its README says it is no longer maintained, so check which MinIO build you run before relying on these settings.

Portainer​

Portainer uses a Custom OAuth provider. Fill in Authorization URL (/login/oauth/authorize), Access token URL (/api/login/oauth/access_token) and Resource URL (/api/userinfo) on your Casdoor host, and set Redirect URL to the Portainer base URL. There is also a Logout URL field. In Portainer CE, Automatic team membership is marked as a Business Edition feature, and the setting that assigns admin rights to groups is only in Business Edition. On CE, users created by automatic provisioning get the standard user role and you promote admins by hand.

Harbor and GitLab​

Harbor shows its redirect URI at the bottom of the OIDC settings page: <harbor-url>/c/oidc/callback. Set OIDC Provider Endpoint to the Casdoor URL, Group Claim Name to groups, and OIDC Admin Group to devops-admins. Harbor reads the group claim from the ID token, which the JWT format provides. You can only switch Harbor from database to OIDC authentication before any local users exist.

GitLab's OIDC docs have a Casdoor section and require Casdoor to be served over HTTPS. The callback is /users/auth/openid_connect/callback. Group-based roles (groups_attribute, admin_groups, required_groups, external_groups) need GitLab Premium or Ultimate.

Tools without OIDC​

For internal dashboards with no login of their own, put them behind Apache APISIX's openid-connect plugin (discovery, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, bearer_only), as in the APISIX guide, or behind nginx as described in Nginx SSO authentication.

One application per tool or a shared one​

A single Casdoor application with every tool's callback in its Redirect URLs works, but one application per tool is easier to run:

  • Each tool gets its own client secret, so a leaked Jenkins secret does not expose Grafana.
  • Token group format, Token format and token expiry are per application, so you can give Argo CD Name (group) without changing another tool's claims.
  • Casdoor checks post_logout_redirect_uri against the Redirect URLs of the application, so each list stays short and specific.

Users still sign in once: after the first login, Casdoor's session cookie lets the next tool's redirect complete without a password prompt.

Вийти​

Casdoor's end-session endpoint is /api/logout, listed as end_session_endpoint in the discovery document. It accepts id_token_hint, post_logout_redirect_uri, client_id and state, and only redirects to a URL listed in the application's Redirect URLs. Signing out of Casdoor ends the Casdoor session and the tokens of that session, but each tool also keeps its own session cookie. Wire up logout in each tool:

  • Jenkins: logoutFromOpenidProvider, with /OicLogout registered.
  • Grafana: signout_redirect_url.
  • Argo CD: logoutURL in oidc.config, for example https://door.example.com/api/logout?id_token_hint={{token}}&post_logout_redirect_uri={{logoutRedirectURL}}.
  • Harbor: OIDC Session Logout.
  • Portainer: Logout URL.

The details of the endpoint are in RP-initiated logout.

Посилання​

  • Gitea: Authentication, admin auth add-oauth
  • Jenkins: OpenId Connect Authentication plugin, configuration reference, Managing security
  • Grafana: Configure generic OAuth2 authentication
  • Argo CD: User management, RBAC, argocd login
  • MinIO: Casdoor quickstart in the MinIO repository
  • Portainer: OAuth authentication
  • Harbor: Configure OIDC provider authentication
  • GitLab: Use OpenID Connect as an authentication provider
  • Apache APISIX: openid-connect plugin

entry.title: DingTalk, WeCom, Lark, Infoflow and WeChat OAuth Login with Casdoor
entry.summary: Sign in with DingTalk, WeCom, Lark/Feishu, Baidu Infoflow and WeChat through Casdoor: app types, QR login, user IDs, email access, corporate tokens, sync.
entry.content:
Casdoor has built-in OAuth providers for DingTalk, WeCom (WeChat Work), Lark (Feishu), Baidu Infoflow and WeChat. You create an app in each vendor's developer console, paste its credentials into a Casdoor provider, and add the provider to your application. Casdoor runs the vendor flow (QR scan on a desktop, or sign-in inside the vendor's own client), fetches the corporate access token where the vendor needs one, and maps the vendor's user ID to a Casdoor user. Your application only talks OIDC to Casdoor and never sees a DingTalk header, a WeCom user_ticket or a WeChat unionid. For DingTalk, WeCom and Lark, a syncer can also import the whole org directory ahead of the first sign-in.

Огляд​

ProviderApp you createWhere users sign inID that links the Casdoor userEmail and phoneDirectory syncer
DingTalkInternal app (AppKey, AppSecret)DingTalk sign-in page, login.dingtalk.comopenId; unionid becomes the usernameFrom the profile, replaced by the corporate directory; treated as verifiedYes
WeComSelf-built app (CorpID, Secret, AgentId), or third-partyWeb login (QR, or quick login from WeCom desktop) or silent sign-in inside WeComuserid (internal), open_userid (third-party)Email only with snsapi_privateinfo; phone not readYes
Lark / FeishuCustom app (App ID, App Secret)Lark sign-in page, Feishu or Lark globalopen_id; username is user_id, else union_id, else open_idYes, if the app has the contact permissionsYes
Baidu InfoflowInternal app (CorpID, Secret, AgentID)Infoflow authorize pageuserid, also the usernameEmailNo
WeChatWebsite app on the Open Platform, plus an Official AccountQR scan on a PC; inside the WeChat browser through the Official Accountunionid, else openidNeitherNo

The setup steps for each are in the docs: DingTalk, WeCom, Lark, Infoflow and WeChat. This post explains what happens behind each one.

What your application sees​

Every provider in the table ends the same way. Casdoor exchanges the vendor's code, finds or creates the user in the organization, and then issues its own authorization code to your app. Your app redeems it at Casdoor's token endpoint and gets a Casdoor ID token and access token, signed with the application's certificate. The claims come from the Casdoor user record: name, display name, email, phone, avatar, groups.

Your backend code is the same for all five. Any OIDC library works; see the OAuth 2.0 and OIDC reference and, for a full walkthrough, Spring Boot SSO with OIDC. If you do need the vendor's own API later, Casdoor stores the provider's access token on the user, as described in OAuth providers.

DingTalk​

Create an internal app on the DingTalk Open Platform and copy its AppKey and AppSecret into the Client ID and Client secret of the provider. The sign-in page sends the user to https://login.dingtalk.com/oauth2/auth with scope=openid and prompt=login consent. After the user confirms, Casdoor makes four calls:

  1. POST https://api.dingtalk.com/v1.0/oauth2/userAccessToken turns the code into a user access token.
  2. GET https://api.dingtalk.com/v1.0/contact/users/me returns the user's openId, unionId, nick, avatar, email and mobile. This needs the Contact.User.Read permission on the app.
  3. POST https://api.dingtalk.com/v1.0/oauth2/accessToken with appKey and appSecret returns the corporate (app) access token.
  4. With that token, topapi/user/getbyunionid maps the unionid to the corporate userid, and topapi/v2/user/get reads the directory record.

If the user is not a member of the organization that owns the app, step 4 fails with DingTalk error 60121 and the sign-in stops. If the directory lookup succeeds, the directory email and mobile replace the personal ones, unionid becomes the username, and the job title is kept as an extra claim.

The corporate access token and its header​

DingTalk has two API generations that take the same token in different places:

GET https://api.dingtalk.com/v1.0/contact/users/me
x-acs-dingtalk-access-token: <token>
POST https://oapi.dingtalk.com/topapi/v2/user/get?access_token=<token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"userid": "<userid>"}

The new API on api.dingtalk.com reads the token only from the x-acs-dingtalk-access-token header. Call it without that header (or with Authorization: Bearer) and it answers AuthenticationFailed.MissingParameter, naming the header. The older oapi.dingtalk.com endpoints still take an access_token query parameter. Casdoor uses both: the header for users/me, the query parameter for the two topapi calls, with the corporate token from v1.0/oauth2/accessToken in both places. DingTalk documents that token as valid for 7,200 seconds and asks callers to cache it per app. DingTalk also marks the old gettoken endpoint as legacy for new apps.

Casdoor counts the email and phone that DingTalk returns as verified, so the default binding rule (email, then phone) can attach a DingTalk sign-in to an existing user. See how Casdoor links accounts.

WeCom (WeChat Work)​

A WeCom provider has a Sub type and a Method:

  • Internal with Normal sends the user to the WeCom web login, login.work.weixin.qq.com/wwlogin/sso/login with login_type=CorpApp. WeCom shows a QR code, or a one-click quick login when WeCom desktop is running and signed in.
  • Internal with Silent uses open.weixin.qq.com/connect/oauth2/authorize with the app's agentid. This is the one to use for pages opened inside the WeCom client.
  • Third-party uses login_type=ServiceApp and the service provider's secret (get_provider_token), then get_login_info, and links the user by open_userid.

For internal apps, Casdoor gets the corporate token from cgi-bin/gettoken with the CorpID and the app Secret, then exchanges the code for the member's userid. A visitor who is not a member comes back with an openid instead, and Casdoor rejects the sign-in. The token is a query parameter on every WeCom call; WeCom says it normally lasts 7,200 seconds and that gettoken is rate limited.

The email address is the part to plan for. WeCom stopped returning avatar, gender, mobile and email from the member read API (user/get) for self-built apps created after 20:00 on 2022-06-20. To get the email, set the provider's scope to snsapi_privateinfo. WeCom then returns a user_ticket, which Casdoor redeems at getuserdetail. WeCom requires the admin to pick the sensitive fields in the app settings and the member to consent, and it never gives these fields to third-party apps. Casdoor does not read the phone number from WeCom.

Lark and Feishu​

Create a custom app on the Feishu Open Platform or the Lark global platform and copy the App ID and App Secret. Turn on Use global endpoint in the provider for Lark (open.larksuite.com); leave it off for Feishu (open.feishu.cn).

Casdoor first gets a tenant_access_token from auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal, then posts the code to authen/v1/access_token with that token in an Authorization: Bearer header. The response carries open_id, union_id, user_id, email, enterprise email and mobile. Feishu returns the sensitive ones only when the app holds the matching permission:

FieldFeishu permission
user_idcontact:user.employee_id:readonly
emailcontact:user.email:readonly
enterprise_emailcontact:user.employee:readonly
mobilecontact:user.phone:readonly

Without them, sign-in still works: the username falls back from user_id to union_id to open_id. Casdoor uses enterprise_email when email is empty and treats both email and phone as verified. Feishu now lists the v1 access_token endpoint as a historical version, but it is still served.

Baidu Infoflow​

Infoflow (如流) is Baidu's workplace app. Register an app in the Infoflow admin, give it address book permissions, and copy the CorpID, Secret and AgentID into the provider with the Internal sub type. The sign-in page goes to https://xpc.im.baidu.com/oauth2/authorize. Casdoor then calls qy.im.baidu.com/api/gettoken with the CorpID and Secret, exchanges the code and AgentID for the member's userid at api/user/getuserinfo, and reads name, avatar and email from api/user/get. The userid becomes both the linked ID and the username, and the email counts as verified. There is no Infoflow syncer, so users are created on first sign-in.

Вхід через WeChat​

WeChat login has two halves, and you usually need both:

  • Web sub type: a website app on the WeChat Open Platform. The PC sign-in page shows a QR code from open.weixin.qq.com/connect/qrconnect with scope=snsapi_login; the user scans it with the WeChat app.
  • Mobile sub type, or the second credential pair of the same provider: an Official Account. Inside the WeChat browser, a QR code is useless, so Casdoor switches to connect/oauth2/authorize with snsapi_userinfo and the Official Account's AppID. If no Official Account is configured, Casdoor tells the user to open the page in an external browser.

WeChat returns no email or phone, only openid, unionid, nickname and avatar. Casdoor links the user by unionid when WeChat sends one, falling back to openid, and also stores the per-app openid. WeChat gives a user the same unionid across all apps and Official Accounts under one Open Platform account, so bind your website app and your Official Account to the same Open Platform account. Otherwise a user who scans on a PC and later signs in on a phone becomes two Casdoor users.

Importing the directory first​

For DingTalk, WeCom and Lark, a syncer can pull users and departments in on a schedule, so accounts exist before anyone signs in and departments become Casdoor groups. Each one uses a corporate token from the vendor's directory API: the DingTalk syncer walks departments recursively, the WeCom syncer falls back to user/list_id and user/get for apps created after 2022-08-15, and the Lark syncer has a Lark platform setting to choose Feishu or Lark global.

The WeCom syncer writes the userid that the WeCom provider links by, so synced users sign in directly. The DingTalk and Lark syncers store the directory userid / user_id, while sign-in links by openId / open_id. Their first sign-in matches through the binding rule on email or phone instead, which works because both providers report those as verified.

QR login and account recovery​

QR login moves the password problem to the phone: if a user loses their WeChat or DingTalk account, they cannot scan. Because each of these identities is linked to a Casdoor user rather than being the user, the user can still sign in with a verification code or reset the password through the forgot-password flow, as long as the application has an email or SMS provider and the user has an address on file. DingTalk and Lark fill that in from the directory; for WeChat, ask for a phone number at sign-up. To show more than one of these options on the page, see sign-in methods.

Посилання​

  • DingTalk: get a user token (userAccessToken, expireIn 7200): https://open.dingtalk.com/document/isvapp-server/obtain-user-token
  • DingTalk: get the access token of an internal app: https://open.dingtalk.com/document/development/obtain-orgapp-token
  • DingTalk: obtain user personal information: https://open.dingtalk.com/document/orgapp-server/tutorial-obtaining-user-personal-information
  • WeCom: get access_token: https://developer.work.weixin.qq.com/document/path/91039
  • WeCom: web login component (wwlogin/sso/login): https://developer.work.weixin.qq.com/document/path/98152
  • WeCom: build the OAuth link and scopes: https://developer.work.weixin.qq.com/document/path/91022
  • WeCom: get sensitive member info (getuserdetail): https://developer.work.weixin.qq.com/document/path/95833
  • WeCom: read member (2022-06-20 field change): https://developer.work.weixin.qq.com/document/path/90196
  • Feishu: get user_access_token (v1) and field permissions: https://open.feishu.cn/document/server-docs/authentication-management/access-token/create-2
  • WeChat: website app login: https://developers.weixin.qq.com/doc/oplatform/Website_App/WeChat_Login/Wechat_Login.html
  • WeChat: UnionID: https://developers.weixin.qq.com/doc/oplatform/Website_App/WeChat_Login/Authorized_Interface_Calling_UnionID.html
  • Casdoor providers: https://github.com/casdoor/casdoor/tree/master/idp

entry.title: Email Provider for Casdoor Verification Codes: Brevo SMTP, Resend, SendGrid, ACS Email and SES
entry.summary: Pick an email provider for Casdoor sign-up codes, password resets and magic links: Brevo SMTP, Resend, SendGrid, Azure ACS Email, Amazon SES and plain SMTP.
entry.content:
Casdoor sends sign-up verification codes, password reset links and magic links through an Email provider. It has native API types for Resend, SendGrid and Azure Communication Services (ACS) Email, a Default SMTP type that works with any SMTP relay (your own server, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Brevo, Amazon SES), and a Custom HTTP Email type for any other HTTP API. If you want a free tier and a short setup, start with Resend or Brevo. If you already run on AWS or Azure, SES or ACS keeps billing in one place. Whichever you pick, the deliverability work is the same: a sender domain with SPF and DKIM that align with the From address.

Огляд варіантів​

Free tiers and prices were checked on 2026-11-02 on each vendor's own pricing page.

ProviderAPI or SMTPFree tier (checked 2026-11-02)Sender domain setupCasdoor type
Your own mail serverSMTPYou run itYou publish SPF, DKIM and DMARC, and need forward and reverse DNS for the IPDefault
Google Workspace (smtp.gmail.com)SMTP with an app passwordPart of the Workspace subscription, 2,000 messages per dayYour Workspace domainDefault
Microsoft 365 (smtp.office365.com)SMTP AUTHPart of the subscriptionYour Microsoft 365 domainDefault
BrevoSMTP relay (smtp-relay.brevo.com)300 emails per dayBrevo code (TXT), DKIM and DMARC recordsDefault
ResendAPI3,000 emails per month, 100 per daySPF and DKIM records generated by Resend, then DMARCResend
SendGridAPI60-day trial, 100 emails per dayDomain authentication: CNAME records for SPF and DKIM, TXT for DMARCSendGrid
Azure Communication Services EmailAPINone listed; $0.00025 per email plus $0.00012 per MBAzure managed subdomain, or a custom domain with SPF and DKIMAzure ACS
Amazon SESSMTP interfaceNo SES-only quota; new AWS accounts get Free Tier credits that SES can useVerified identity for every From addressDefault
Any other HTTP APIHTTPDepends on the serviceDepends on the serviceCustom HTTP Email

The Email providers overview in the docs lists the same types and the fields each one uses.

SMTP: your own server, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365​

The Default type takes a host, port, username and password. SSL mode Auto uses implicit TLS on port 465 and STARTTLS on other ports, which covers almost every relay below.

With your own server, SPF, DKIM signing, reverse DNS and IP reputation are all yours. Google requires valid forward and reverse DNS (PTR) records for the sending IP.

Google Workspace documents smtp.gmail.com on port 465 or 587, signed in with the full Workspace address and an app password, with a limit of 2,000 messages per day.

Microsoft 365 is the one to avoid for new setups. Casdoor's SMTP provider signs in with a username and password, which is Basic authentication for SMTP AUTH. Microsoft has announced plans to retire Basic authentication for SMTP AUTH in Exchange Online, and has already turned SMTP AUTH off in tenants that weren't using it. Check the latest timeline in the announcement below before you build on it.

Brevo SMTP​

Brevo sends transactional mail through a standard SMTP relay, so it uses the Default type. Most setup problems come from the Brevo SMTP login:

  • The server is smtp-relay.brevo.com, on port 587, 465 or 2525. Port 465 needs SSL, which Auto handles.
  • The SMTP login is not always your account email. Depending on when the account was created, it is either your login email or a generated address like [ID]@smtp-brevo.com, and it is shown on the SMTP page in Brevo. Changing your account email doesn't change it.
  • The password is an SMTP key, not an API key.

In Casdoor, set Type to Default and put those values in Host, Port, Username and Password. The Brevo guide has screenshots. For the domain, Brevo asks for its own TXT verification record, DKIM and DMARC; SPF is only needed with a dedicated IP.

Resend​

The Resend type needs only an API key in Secret key, plus a From address on a verified domain. Leave Host, Port and Username empty. Casdoor formats the sender as Name <address> from From name, or from the organization's display name when From name is empty.

Two things to know before you test. First, the shared onboarding@resend.dev sender can only send to the email address of your own Resend account; any other recipient gets a 403. Second, verifying your own domain means adding the SPF and DKIM records Resend generates, and Resend recommends sending from a subdomain to keep its reputation separate. The free plan covers 3,000 emails a month with a cap of 100 per day; the Pro plan starts at $20 a month for 50,000. See the Resend guide.

SendGrid​

The SendGrid type uses an API key. Leave Host and Endpoint empty and Casdoor uses SendGrid's standard send API; fill both only if you need a different endpoint. Casdoor treats anything but 202 Accepted as a failure and shows the error messages SendGrid returns, which helps when a sender isn't verified yet.

SendGrid's pricing page lists a 60-day free trial at 100 emails a day, then Essentials from $19.95 a month. Domain authentication with automated security adds a CNAME for SPF and DKIM and a TXT record for DMARC. See the SendGrid guide.

ACS Email (Azure Communication Services)​

The Azure ACS type takes the resource endpoint as Host and the access key as Secret key; Casdoor signs each request with that key. Azure gives you a one-click managed subdomain under azurecomm.net with authentication already set up, and Microsoft suggests using it for development and switching to a custom domain, with its SPF and DKIM records, for launch. There is no free tier on the pricing page: $0.00025 per email plus $0.00012 per MB transferred. See the Azure ACS guide.

Amazon SES​

Casdoor has no SES API type, so use the SES SMTP interface with the Default type. The host is the Region's SMTP endpoint, such as email-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com; SES accepts STARTTLS on 25, 587 or 2587 and implicit TLS on 465 or 2465. The SMTP username and password are SMTP credentials you generate in SES. They are not your AWS access keys, and they are different in each Region.

New accounts start in the SES sandbox: mail goes only to verified addresses, at most 200 messages per 24 hours and one per second. Request production access before real users sign up. SES charges $0.10 per 1,000 outbound emails at its à la carte rate, with no minimum fee.

Custom HTTP Email​

For a service without a native type, Custom HTTP Email sends fromAddress, fromName, toAddress (or toAddresses for several recipients), subject and content as a form or JSON body, with headers you define. You can rename each field to match the target API. Casdoor counts only HTTP 200 as success, so an API that answers 202 Accepted shows up as an error; a small adapter in front fixes that. See Send email through your own HTTP API.

Deliverability basics for auth mail​

Verification codes are useless if they land in spam. The rules that matter:

  • SPF and DKIM. Google requires every sender to Gmail to use SPF or DKIM. Above 5,000 messages a day it requires both, plus DMARC (a p=none policy is accepted). Set up all three from the start.
  • Alignment. The domain in the From header must match the SPF domain or the DKIM domain, or DMARC fails. This is why each provider makes you verify the domain you send from.
  • A separate subdomain. Yahoo recommends separating transactional mail from marketing mail by IP or DKIM domain, and Resend recommends subdomains. Something like auth.example.com keeps a bad newsletter from hurting your password resets.
  • TLS and spam rate. Google requires TLS and asks you to keep the reported spam rate below 0.3%, ideally below 0.1%.
  • No unsubscribe header needed. Google's FAQ says one-click unsubscribe applies to marketing mail, and names password reset messages as an example of transactional mail that is excluded.
  • Simple content. Casdoor sends the template as one HTML body, without a separate plain-text part, for every built-in type. Keep the HTML light, put the code in plain text, and show the full link as text next to the button, as Casdoor's built-in magic link email does. Use your Casdoor origin directly rather than a link shortener, so the link domain matches your brand.

Configure and test the provider in Casdoor​

  1. Go to Identity > Providers, add a provider, set Category to Email and choose the Type from the table above.
  2. Set From address and, optionally, From name.
  3. Write Email title and Email content. The content can use %s for the code, %{user.friendlyName} for the user's name, and %link inside a <reset-link> block for the password reset link. Magic link emails use %link and %expireTime; if your content has no %link, Casdoor sends its own magic link email instead. The templates section has examples. One thing to edit: the default template says the code is valid for 5 minutes, but codes and magic links expire after verificationCodeTimeout in conf/app.conf, which defaults to 10 minutes.
  4. Click Test SMTP Connection to open a connection without sending (SMTP types only), then enter an address in Test Email and click Send Testing Email. The test uses the values in the form, saved or not, with %s replaced by 123456 and the reset link block removed.
  5. Add the provider to the application with a rule such as Signup, Forget Password, Magic link or All. You can use different providers for different rules. See Add providers to an application.
  6. Set origin in conf/app.conf. Without it, unless the request comes in on a loopback host such as localhost, Casdoor leaves the reset link out of password reset emails and refuses to send magic links. See Sign in with a magic link.

For local development, point a Default provider at a fake SMTP server instead of a real account; MailHog vs Mailpit covers that setup.

entry.title: How to Host Static Files on a CDN with Casdoor: S3, MinIO, Azure Blob and Other Storage Providers
entry.summary: Where Casdoor keeps avatars and uploaded files (local disk, Amazon S3, MinIO, Azure Blob, GCS, OSS, COS, Synology) and how to serve them through a CDN.
entry.content:
To host static files on a CDN, put them in object storage (Amazon S3, MinIO, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage, Alibaba Cloud OSS or Tencent Cloud COS), make the CDN pull from that bucket as its origin, and hand out URLs on the CDN's domain. In Casdoor this is one setting: create a storage provider for the bucket and put the CDN address in its Domain field. Casdoor uploads avatars and other files through the provider's API and saves URLs that start with that domain. Casdoor's own frontend can come from a CDN as well, through frontendCdnUrl and staticBaseUrl in app.conf.

Storage providers at a glance​

A storage provider decides where Casdoor writes uploaded files: user avatars, ID card images, terms-of-use pages, and anything uploaded on the Resources page. You add the provider to an application, and uploads made in that application go to it. The storage provider overview lists all the types. This table covers the ones people usually ask about:

StorageCasdoor provider typeDoes Casdoor use the S3 API?Self-hostableHow the public URL is set
Local file systemLocal File SystemNo, plain files on diskYes, it is the Casdoor serverServed by Casdoor under /files/. Domain is read-only
Amazon S3AWS S3YesNoDomain: the bucket URL or a CloudFront domain. Endpoint (Intranet): a VPC endpoint
MinIOMinIOYes, with path-style requestsYesDomain: the MinIO URL followed by the bucket name, or a CDN domain
Alibaba Cloud OSSAliyun OSSNo, the OSS SDKNoDomain: a CDN domain. Left empty, it becomes bucket.endpoint. Endpoint (Intranet): the internal endpoint
Tencent Cloud COSTencent Cloud COSNo, the COS APINoDomain: a CDN domain
Azure Blob StorageAzure BlobNo, the Blob APINoDomain: a custom or Front Door domain. Casdoor adds the container name to the path
Google Cloud StorageGoogle Cloud StorageNo, Google's Go clientNoDomain: left empty, it becomes https://storage.googleapis.com. Casdoor adds the bucket name to the path
Synology NASSynologyNo, the DSM File Station APIYesNo Domain field. The URL is based on Endpoint

Casdoor also supports Qiniu Cloud Kodo, CUCloud OSS, and Casdoor, which stores files in another Casdoor instance. The per-provider guides for Amazon S3, MinIO, Azure Blob, Google Cloud Storage, Alibaba Cloud OSS, Tencent Cloud COS, Synology NAS and the local file system show which value goes in which field.

Endpoint vs. Domain​

These two fields do different jobs, and most CDN problems come from mixing them up.

  • Endpoint is the address Casdoor uses to talk to the storage API: upload, delete, list. The CDN is not involved.
  • Endpoint (Intranet) replaces Endpoint when isCloudIntranet = true is set in app.conf. That keeps upload traffic on the provider's internal network when Casdoor runs in the same cloud. The field appears for AWS S3, Aliyun OSS, Azure Blob and CUCloud OSS.
  • Domain is the base of the URL that Casdoor saves and that browsers request. If you have a CDN, its domain goes here.
  • Path prefix is put in front of every object key. With a prefix of casdoor, an avatar ends up under casdoor/avatar/....

Casdoor builds the file URL from the scheme and host of Domain, then the path of Domain, then the path prefix, then the file path. A Domain without a scheme gets https://. The path part of Domain also becomes part of the object key, so https://cdn.example.com/casdoor/ stores files under casdoor/ in the bucket. For Azure Blob and Google Cloud Storage, Casdoor adds the container or bucket name as the first path segment after the host. Your CDN needs to serve that path.

If Domain is empty, Casdoor fills it in from the provider's endpoint the first time it uses the provider, and saves it. Sometimes the result works, as with OSS and GCS. Sometimes it doesn't: for an S3 endpoint without the bucket name, or for MinIO, where path-style requests put the bucket name in the path, the generated URL misses the bucket. Set Domain yourself, upload one test avatar, and open the URL Casdoor returns before anyone else uses it.

The provider that Casdoor uses for avatars it copies from social logins comes from defaultStorageProvider in app.conf. It is the name of a provider owned by admin (see the configuration reference):

defaultStorageProvider = provider_storage_s3
isCloudIntranet = false

Public buckets, private buckets and signed URLs​

Casdoor saves one plain, permanent URL in the user's avatar field and in the resource record. It doesn't create signed or expiring URLs for these files. So whatever is at Domain has to answer an anonymous GET. There are two ways to do that.

Make the objects public. With AWS S3 and MinIO, Casdoor uploads every object with the public-read canned ACL. With Aliyun OSS, the client library does the same by default. On S3 this conflicts with the defaults for new buckets: according to AWS, new buckets use the Bucket owner enforced setting, which disables ACLs, and an upload that sets an ACL such as public-read fails with AccessControlListNotSupported. That is why the Amazon S3 guide has you turn on ACLs and turn off Block all public access. On OSS, an object ACL takes precedence over the bucket ACL, so a public-read object can be read even in a private bucket. MinIO doesn't use the ACL for anonymous reads. It uses a bucket policy:

mc anonymous set download myminio/casdoor

Azure needs anonymous access allowed on the storage account and the container set to the Blob access level. Google Cloud Storage needs the Storage Object Viewer role (roles/storage.objectViewer) granted to allUsers on the bucket.

Keep the bucket private and let only the CDN read it. The CDN signs its requests to the origin, and viewers go through the CDN without a signature. Each vendor has its own version:

  • CloudFront has origin access control (OAC). AWS requires Bucket owner enforced for OAC, or Bucket owner preferred if you need ACLs.
  • Alibaba Cloud CDN can fetch from a private OSS bucket after you authorize it.
  • Tencent Cloud CDN has origin-pull authentication for private COS buckets.
  • Azure Front Door Premium can reach a storage account over Private Link.
  • Google's Cloud CDN guide covers private bucket access too, where the Storage Object Viewer role goes to a service account instead of allUsers.

This hides the bucket's own URL, but the files are still public through the CDN. With the AWS S3 and Aliyun OSS types, the objects also stay readable at their bucket URLs, because of the public-read ACL that Casdoor sets.

If avatars must not be public at all, a CDN in front of object storage is the wrong tool. Keep those files on a storage type you control, and limit who can reach that host.

Cache headers and the avatar trap​

On S3 and MinIO, Casdoor sets Content-Type from the file extension when it uploads. It doesn't set Cache-Control on any provider. That means the CDN's default TTL applies. On CloudFront, objects without Cache-Control are cached for the default TTL, which is 24 hours when you don't use a cache policy. To control this per object, add Cache-Control metadata in the bucket. For a whole path, use a cache rule on the CDN.

Avatars need a short TTL. When a user changes their picture, Casdoor writes the new file to the same key, avatar/<organization>/<username>.<extension>, and saves the same URL. A long TTL means people see the old picture until it expires or until you purge or invalidate that path. Other uploads get a numbered suffix (-1, -2, ...) when the name is already taken, so a new upload gets a new URL and can be cached for a long time.

A layout that works:

PathSuggested caching
avatar/*Short TTL (minutes), or purge on change
resource/* and other uploadsLong TTL
Hashed frontend assets (assets/*)Very long TTL. The file name changes on every build

Casdoor's own frontend on a CDN​

Separate from user uploads, there are three ways to move Casdoor's own static files off the Casdoor server.

frontendCdnUrl. Use this if you install the frontend from the casdoor-web npm package. Point it at an npm CDN, for example:

frontendCdnUrl = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/{name}@{version}"

Casdoor reads the package name and version from the package.json in the build folder. It rewrites the script and stylesheet links in index.html to that CDN and keeps the local paths as a fallback. If a file fails to load, the browser loads it from Casdoor, and a cookie keeps that browser on local files for the rest of the session. A frontend you build yourself has no such package.json, so the setting has no effect on it.

The deployment script. For a frontend you build from source, Host the frontend files on a CDN explains deployment/deploy_test.go. It uploads web/build/assets/ through one of your storage providers and points index.html at the provider's Domain, which must end with /. Vite hashes these file names, so they suit the long TTL in the table above.

staticBaseUrl. This sets where default images such as logos, provider icons and the default avatar come from. The default is https://cdn.casbin.org, which serves the casbin/static repository. On a network without internet access, serve a copy of that repository yourself and point staticBaseUrl at it, as described in Host static files on an intranet.

Picking one​

  • One server, small user base: Local File System. Mount the files directory on a volume if Casdoor runs in a container. Casdoor sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and a sandboxing Content-Security-Policy with these files, so an uploaded HTML or SVG file can't run script on your Casdoor domain.
  • Self-hosted and S3-shaped: MinIO. It is also the type the docs suggest for other S3-compatible stores.
  • Already on a cloud: use that cloud's object storage and CDN, set Endpoint (Intranet) where Casdoor runs in the same cloud, and set Domain to the CDN.
